legal.headline: Supreme Court’s new sequencing of matters in cause list: fresh and early-hearing matters in Part A, after-notice in Part B
legal.hook: SCBA informs the revised arrangement of Cause List, to be published in 2 parts, ending the practice of assigning a sequence to matters at 10:30 a.m
legal.summary: The Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) has notified a revised arrangement for the Supreme Court of India’s cause list sequencing. Under the updated mechanism, the cause list will be published in two distinct sections: Part A will feature fresh admission matters and early-hearing cases, while Part B will contain after-notice matters. This operational change officially eliminates the previous practice of dynamically assigning item sequences to listed matters at 10:30 a.m. on the morning of hearings, providing counsel and litigants with structured, predictable cause lists ahead of court sessions.
legal.contextNote: This administrative overhaul, issued under the practice directions supplementing the Supreme Court Rules, 2013, standardizes court time management across all benches. (1) Litigation teams filing fresh Special Leave Petitions (SLPs) or statutory appeals (e.g., under Section 62 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code or Section 53T of the Competition Act) can expect Part A fresh matters to be taken up systematically before after-notice cases, streamlining morning mentionings and arguments. (2) In-house counsel managing Senior Advocate briefings must recalibrate scheduling, as Part B after-notice matters will no longer risk being called unexpectedly during the opening 10:30 a.m. slot. (3) Corporate legal departments tracking high-stakes regulatory or commercial matters can now map court clashes and advocate availability across multiple benches with significantly higher procedural certainty.
